additions.name: China Telecom Innovation Incubation (South) Base — AIDC computing infrastructure in Buildings A1, A3 and A4

status.summary: On 16 October 2026 the Guangdong Energy Bureau published energy-review opinion 粤能许可〔2026〕85号, approving in principle the energy report of China Telecom Corporation Limited Guangdong Branch for an intelligent-computing (AIDC) infrastructure project at parcel ZSCN-D4-1 of its Innovation Incubation (South) Base in Sino-Singapore Guangzhou Knowledge City. The project fits out the campus's existing Buildings A1, A3 and A4 with 71,132 kW of total construction power (28,452.8 standard-rack equivalents; 2,730 racks), electromechanical installation and server racking only, with production expected in June 2028. This dated government record identifies the project and supports announced status. An energy review is not development consent; no fit-out work, completion or operation is established, and capacity and timing are plans.

locator.precision: Official Guangzhou planning-publicity register marker of the October 2022 as-built verification of machine-room buildings A3 and A4 (穗规划资源核实〔2022〕2596号) on parcel ZSCN-D4-1. Locates the China Telecom campus through two of the three AIDC buildings; not a building footprint, parcel centroid, entrance or construction extent, and it does not locate Building A1.
locator.identity_review: The register record names 知识城南起步区ZSCN-D4-1地块中国电信创新孵化(南方)基地机房(自编号A3和A4), built by China Telecom Group Guangdong Branch south of planned KS2 Road and east of the Yongjiu Expressway, the same parcel (ZSCN-D4-1) and base (中国电信创新孵化（南方）基地) as the energy review, whose project reuses Buildings A1, A3 and A4. Published lnglat 113.536462197222,23.318173 is taken as printed (rounded to nine decimals); the page plots it in wkid 4326 on Tianditu CGCS2000 tiles. Read as WGS84 it falls among the flat-roofed machine-room buildings of the walled campus in Esri World Imagery; the GCJ-02 alternative would lie about 611 m west-north-west at the expressway edge. Five later register records for the same base (2023 detailed plan, 2024 permits and January 2026 verifications for research buildings B1-B3 and canopies) lie 32-129 m from the point. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-23-cn-south-p2-guangzhou-planning-register-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: No datum or positional accuracy is stated in the record; the page plots it as geographic wkid 4326 on Tianditu CGCS2000 tiles, and the WGS84 reading is supported only by a qualitative check against Esri World Imagery (the GCJ-02 alternative falls about 610-630 m away on land without the described buildings). Placement rules for register markers are undocumented; markers of other records for the same parcel lie up to 160 m apart, so the point locates the parcel, not a building. Decimal places are publication precision, not accuracy.

additions.name: QTS Cambois Phase 2 - two data centre buildings (Northumberland reserved matters 26/03028/REM)
additions.site_identity_review: The notice places 26/03028/REM on 'Phase 2 of the data centre campus' at the 'Land at Former Power Station Site on Northern Side of Cambois' and makes it pursuant to outline permission 24/04112/OUTES. The Environment Agency-hosted QTS Project Wind Environmental Setting and Site Design Report (Cundall, November 2025; the evidence behind this site's existing campus locator) states that QTS Data Centres is developing the Cambois Campus on the former coal-stock yards of Blyth Power Station and that 24/04112/OUTES is the outline permission for the entire Cambois Campus site (up to ten data centre buildings, up to 540,000 m2 GIA), granted on 8 May 2025, with enabling works approved under 25/01725/REM. The 9 October 2026 council notice ties the same outline reference and the same applicant, Renaissance Land Limited (recorded in the Atlas source record as the Blackstone-owned entity financing the QTS project), to the former power station site at NE22 7BL, the postcode of the Environment Agency permit application for QTS Project Wind (Rainton Construction Limited, EPR/JP3321LF/A001). Phase 2 is therefore a further phase of the existing QTS Cambois campus, not a new site; it is distinct from the existing campus-wide record and from the 2026 earthworks record, and from Phase A (the first two data centre units).

status.summary: Northumberland County Council's statutory notice dated 25 September 2026 publicises reserved matters application 26/03028/REM by Renaissance Land Limited for appearance, landscaping, layout and scale of two data centre buildings with ancillary offices (Use Class B8) and associated landscaping and infrastructure on Phase 2 of the Cambois data centre campus, pursuant to outline permission 24/04112/OUTES. This dated government record identifies the Phase 2 project, so it is announced as of 25 September 2026. The reserved matters are undecided in the notice, so permitted status is not asserted for Phase 2 (the 2025 outline consent alone leaves its detailed design unapproved and predates the window), and no works on Phase 2 are implied.

locator.identity_review: Reuses the existing QTS Cambois campus point exactly: the Environment Agency-hosted applicant report's approximate centre of the wider Cambois Campus (NGR NZ 29820 84164, transformed once), with its pinned geometry and geometry-identity evidence. That report defines the wider campus as the 24/04112/OUTES outline site, which the Phase 2 reserved matters application sits within. The point does not locate the two Phase 2 buildings or their plot; no Phase 2 layout plan was read (Northumberland's planning portal disallows all crawling).

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 23 October 2026 against all sites, projects and evidence, the 231 source records and the identity mapping of verified_construction_core/2026-10-23-research-fiftysixth (re-read from site/config.json; the base moved from fiftythird to fiftysixth during this pass) and re-screened by the verifier against verified_construction_core/2026-10-23-research-fiftyseventh (no Phase 2, 26/03028/REM or 24/04112/OUTES record), every other queue fragment's changes and holds, all sources/*-holds.json and claims.tsv, for QTS, Cambois, Project Wind, Renaissance Land, 24/04112/OUTES, 26/03028/REM and Phase 2. The only matches are the existing QTS Cambois site (campus-wide record imported:semiconductor-atlas:qts-cambois-blyth and curated:qts-cambois-data-centre-campus:2026-earthworks), whose source record notes phase one's first two buildings (reserved matters approved December 2025) and ten planned buildings, and the separate TBC Partners Cambois proposal on Factory Road. No record or queued addition names Phase 2 or 26/03028/REM. Atlas records within 2 km: the QTS Cambois site point and its earthworks project (0 km, the host campus), and the imported QTS campus project and TBC Partners Cambois locality points (both 0.65 km, the Cambois village reference point). The nearest other site, Sembcorp Wilton International, is 68.5 km away. Earlier holds that checked QTS Cambois refreshes did not consider Phase 2.
additions.successor_review: The notice invites representations within 21 days of 25 September 2026 and records no decision. Northumberland's planning portal (publicaccess.northumberland.gov.uk) disallows all agents in robots.txt and was not read, so a decision issued in October 2026 cannot be excluded; it would be a later, separate observation. The council's 9 October 2026 notice (26/02919/FUL, temporary 60kV substation for construction and early operation of the campus) and the 4 September 2026 notice (26/02818/FUL, 11/33kV temporary substations) concern grid infrastructure and do not report Phase 2 works. QTS's news sitemap (re-read 23 October 2026) lists no Cambois item other than the October 2025 social-value release. Phase 2 stays announced as of 25 September 2026.

status.summary: Harworth Group's stand-alone data-centre pipeline release of 19 August 2026 states that its first hyperscale data-centre transaction is a GBP 106m two-plot powered land sale at Skelton Grange to Microsoft with a development agreement for enabling works, and that the Skelton Grange transaction is progressing towards completion. This dated landowner disclosure shows the Microsoft data-centre development at Skelton Grange to be a live, named project on 19 August 2026. It reports no planning decision notice, no start of enabling works and no building stage, so the status stays announced.

status_updates.identity_review: Same project as the existing record 'Microsoft Skelton Grange datacentre campus, Leeds', whose 27 April 2026 status comes from Harworth's release on the resolution to grant planning consent for Microsoft's hyperscale data centre and industrial space at Skelton Grange. The 19 August release names Microsoft and Skelton Grange and describes the same powered land transaction (two plots, GBP 106m, development agreement for enabling works). No new phase, building or site is implied, and the record's existing locator, scope and capacity are unchanged.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 27 April 2026 observation. Harworth's half-year results announcement of 9 September 2026 (local harworth-hy2026-results-20260909.html, sha256 64463acd...) repeats that the final plot sale to Microsoft at Skelton Grange is progressing towards completion; it is not used as the observation because it is a period report (six months to 30 June 2026), following the thirty-first holds' treatment of that RNS. Harworth's post list re-read on 23 October 2026 (local harworth-wp-posts-20261023.json) has nothing after 18 September 2026 (a St Helens land sale); no completion of the Microsoft plot sale, decision notice or start of works at Skelton Grange has been announced. Leeds City Council's planning portal is robots-disallowed and was not read, so a decision notice issued after the April resolution to grant cannot be excluded; permitted status is not asserted. The 19 August 2026 announced observation is kept.

context_updates.identity_review: Same QTS Cambois campus as the existing record (former Blyth Power Station site, 'Project Wind'). The 9 October 2026 notice names the proposed Cambois Data Centre Campus with outline reference 24/04112/OUTES at the former power station site, NE22 7BL; the Environment Agency-hosted Project Wind report identifies 24/04112/OUTES as the outline permission for QTS's entire Cambois Campus, and the Atlas source record names the applicant, Renaissance Land Limited, as the Blackstone-owned entity financing the QTS project. The 4 September 2026 notice is by the same applicant for the same named campus, on land east of Sleekburn Business Centre, West Sleekburn, an address separate from the former power station site (whether it lies within the outline application boundary was not established).
context_updates.summary: Two Northumberland County Council notices publicise Renaissance Land Limited's applications for temporary grid infrastructure 'for the construction and early operation of the proposed Cambois Data Centre Campus': 26/02818/FUL for 11/33kV temporary substations at West Sleekburn (notice dated 4 September 2026) and 26/02919/FUL for a 60kV temporary substation on the former power station site (notice dated 9 October 2026). Power-readiness context only: both are undecided applications, not consents or completed grid works, and the campus's status, observation date, location and capacity are unchanged.
